Treat every reported NAPCS product as an operating-market definition

Include complete-operation, property-management, holding-company, consulting, construction-management, farm-management, food-service-management, and computer-facilities-management activities despite explicit NAICS cross-references
analysis_summary: The defensible family core is outsourced, multi-function day-to-day office administration for client businesses, delivered without operating staff for complete business operations. The NAICS definition directly supports that horizontal boundary and explicitly excludes complete-operation models and several adjacent industries. Medical, dental, hotel, motel, and other named administration labels are recognized in the manual index, but the pack does not resolve whether their buyer, workflow, workforce, economics, and AI workflow warrant separate vertical markets; medical and dental seeds are therefore retained as provisional vertical inputs rather than folded into the horizontal core. The linked NAPCS records show products sold by the industry, not the family operating boundary; they are retained as non-market source identities or outside-family product identities.

proposed_markets.ambient_ai_workflow: AI may assist billing, recordkeeping, scheduling, personnel administration, document handling, and logistics coordination; material implementation detail is not directly evidenced.
proposed_markets.boundary: Includes horizontal multi-function, day-to-day office administration performed for others on contract or fee.
